stem: Faucet A can fill a water tank in 4 hours. Faucet B can fill the same tank in 12 hours. If both faucets are open, how many hours will it take to fill the tank?
hints: Two faucets fill faster than one. The answer must be less than 4 hours.
Faucet A fills 1/4 of the tank per hour. Faucet B fills 1/12 of it per hour.
Add 1/4 + 1/12 using 12 as the bottom number, simplify, then flip the fraction to get the hours.

solution.methodName: Work rates: rate = 1 ÷ time, then add the rates

steps.action: Let t = the hours needed with both faucets open.
Rates: A fills 1/4 of the tank per hour, and B fills 1/12 per hour.

steps.why: Multiply the top and bottom by 3.

steps.action: Add the rates: 3/12 + 1/12 = 4/12 = 1/3 of the tank per hour.
steps.why: Divide the top and bottom of 4/12 by 4.

steps.action: Check: in 3 hours A fills 3 × 1/4 = 3/4 and B fills 3 × 1/12 = 1/4. 3/4 + 1/4 = 1 full tank. It takes 3 hours.

trapNotes.8: This is the average of 4 and 12. Two faucets together fill faster than faucet A alone, so the answer must be less than 4.
trapNotes.16: This adds the times, 4 + 12. Add the rates (1/4 + 1/12), not the hours.
trapNotes.1/3: This is the combined rate, 1/3 of the tank per hour. Flip it to get the time: 1 ÷ 1/3 = 3.
